holidays.name: Send a Card to a Friend Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to dusting off the stamps and mailing an actual paper card to a pal, just because. No special occasion required, only the radical act of using the postal service for friendship.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of greeting card and stationery enthusiasts promoting old-fashioned correspondence in the digital age.
holidays.funFact: Americans send billions of greeting cards each year, and Valentine's Day is one of the biggest card-sending occasions, which makes this day a handy warm-up.

holidays.name: Fettuccine Alfredo Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the creamy, buttery, cheesy pasta dish that makes carb lovers swoon. Participants are encouraged to twirl, slurp, and not think about the calorie count.
holidays.origin: The dish was created in Rome by restaurateur Alfredo di Lelio around 1914, reportedly to tempt his wife Ines, who had lost her appetite after childbirth. The food holiday honors this origin.
holidays.funFact: The original Roman version used just fresh fettuccine, butter, and Parmigiano-Reggiano. The heavy cream version is largely an American addition, and many Italians barely recognize it.

holidays.name: Wave All Your Fingers at Your Neighbor Day
holidays.description: A day for greeting neighbors with a cheerful, full-hand finger wiggle wave instead of the boring standard wave. It is basically a friendliness challenge for your street.
holidays.origin: Believed to be a whimsical unofficial holiday created to encourage community friendliness and break the awkward silence between people living next door to each other.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study social behavior note that even small gestures like waving can increase feelings of belonging in a neighborhood.

holidays.name: Charles Dickens Day
holidays.description: A literary celebration of the birthday of one of history's most famous novelists, creator of Scrooge, Oliver Twist, and Miss Havisham. Fans mark it with readings, tea, and dramatic exclamations of 'Bah, humbug!'
holidays.origin: Charles Dickens was born on February 7, 1812, in Portsmouth, England. Literary societies and fans around the world mark his birthday each year.
holidays.funFact: Dickens was a devoted performer who gave public readings of his work so dramatic that audience members were known to faint, and he walked up to 20 miles at night to cure his insomnia.

holidays.name: Rose Day
holidays.description: The first day of Valentine's Week in India and some other countries, when people give roses to crushes, friends, and loved ones to kick off a week of romantic gestures.
holidays.origin: Rose Day began as part of the modern Valentine's Week tradition that spread across South Asia, with each day from February 7 to 14 assigned a theme such as Propose Day, Chocolate Day, and Teddy Day.
holidays.funFact: Different rose colors carry different meanings in Rose Day tradition: red for love, yellow for friendship, pink for admiration, and white for peace.
